subject: [PATCH 0/2] mm/mempolicy: stop copying state in the interleave paths

reviews.author: Rakie Kim
reviews.summary: Reviewer noted that matching two reads of a nodemask does not guarantee a correct distribution, and agreed with the decision to keep things simple by clamping the walk to a single pass.
reviews.raw_body:
Fair enough. Your example makes the point. The mask can change after
the sum as well, so matching the two reads does not get us a correct
distribution either. Keeping it simple sounds right to me.

Please feel free to add the following to this patch:
Reviewed-by: Rakie Kim <rakie.kim@sk.com>

Thanks for walking through it.

Rakie Kim

2026-09-07.patch_summary: This patch eliminates unnecessary copies of nodemask and node weights in the interleave paths of the Linux kernel's memory policy module. It achieves this by using SRCU to pin node weights in place, operating directly on pol->nodes for nodemasks, and clamping the walk to a single pass. The changes improve performance but may introduce a small trade-off in distribution accuracy during rebind operations.
